subject: Physics
description: Static, kinetic, rolling friction; coefficient; applications; lubricants

questions.stem: For the same pair of surfaces and the same normal force, the LARGEST friction is usually:

options.option_text: Kinetic friction during steady sliding motion
Maximum static friction just before motion starts
Rolling friction of a wheel on the same surface
Air drag on the object at low velocity

questions.explanation: For the same surfaces, μ_static > μ_kinetic > μ_rolling. That's why a stationary object takes more force to start moving than to keep moving once moving. Rolling friction is ~1/100 of sliding — the reason wheels were transformative. Distractor 1 — common confusion between static and kinetic. Distractor 3 — rolling is the smallest. Distractor 4 — air drag at low speed is negligible compared with surface friction.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The coefficient of friction (μ) between two given surfaces depends most directly on:

options.option_text: The mass of the object placed on the surface
The roughness and material of the contact surfaces
The macroscopic area of contact between the bodies
The speed at which the object is being moved

questions.explanation: μ depends on what the two surfaces are made of and their roughness/lubrication. It does NOT depend on mass directly (mass changes normal force N, but F = μN keeps μ constant) or contact area (Amontons's 2nd law). For moderate speeds, μ is approximately speed-independent. Distractor 1 — μ stays constant when mass changes. Distractor 3 — area independence is counter-intuitive but well-established. Distractor 4 — μ varies very weakly with speed at everyday speeds.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: A 5 kg block rests on a horizontal floor with coefficient of static friction 0.4 (g = 10 m/s²). The minimum horizontal force required to start it moving is:

options.option_text: 5 N

questions.explanation: Normal force N = mg = 5 × 10 = 50 N. Maximum static friction = μ_s × N = 0.4 × 50 = 20 N. Force just exceeding 20 N starts motion. Distractor 10 N = mg/5, an arbitrary fraction. Distractor 5 N = the mass itself, no force calculation. Distractor 50 N = the normal force without applying μ.

questions.stem: Ball bearings reduce friction in a rotating shaft mainly by:

options.option_text: Increasing the surface area of the contact zone
Replacing sliding contact with low-friction rolling contact
Eliminating all friction between the moving parts
Dissipating frictional heat into the surroundings quickly

questions.explanation: Ball bearings let the inner shaft roll on small spheres rather than slide directly against the outer race. Rolling friction is ~1/100 of sliding friction → power loss + wear drop dramatically. Used in wheels, motors, pulleys, machine spindles. Distractor 1 — increasing area doesn't lower μ. Distractor 3 — friction is reduced, not eliminated. Distractor 4 — heat dissipation is incidental, not the primary mechanism.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: Without friction, which set of everyday actions would become impossible?

options.option_text: Heating water on a gas stove and boiling it to steam
Walking on the ground, writing with a pen, braking a vehicle
Throwing a ball upward and watching it return to earth
Filling a bucket from a tap and letting water settle

questions.explanation: Walking — the foot pushes back on the ground; the ground pushes forward on you via friction. Writing — pen tip drags on paper, depositing ink. Braking — pads grip the rotor (or tyre grips road) by friction. Distractor 1 — heating is by combustion, not friction. Distractor 3 — gravity, not friction, is what brings the ball back. Distractor 4 — gravity drives water flow; friction is incidental.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: Lubricants such as engine oil reduce friction primarily by:

options.option_text: Cooling the rubbing surfaces well below room temperature
Forming a thin fluid film that separates the two surfaces
Hardening the asperities on each contacting surface
Increasing the normal force pressing the surfaces together

questions.explanation: A lubricant forms a thin layer that prevents direct contact between asperities; sliding now occurs within the lubricant film, which has very low internal shear resistance. Engine oil, gearbox grease, graphite, and MoS₂ work this way. Distractor 1 — cooling is incidental. Distractor 3 — hardening would not reduce friction. Distractor 4 — increasing N would INCREASE friction (F = μN).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: A road is BANKED at the curve so that, at the design speed, the centripetal force is supplied by:

options.option_text: Static friction alone, with the road kept perfectly horizontal
The horizontal component of the normal force on the tilted road
The weight of the vehicle pulling it inward toward the curve
Air drag pushing the car sideways through the bend

questions.explanation: On a banked road, the horizontal component of the normal force provides the centripetal force at the design speed; friction is then NOT needed. Above or below design speed, friction supplies the remainder. Banking thus reduces friction demand → safer at higher speeds and on icy/wet roads. Distractor 1 describes a flat road where friction alone supplies centripetal force. Distractor 3 — gravity acts vertically downward, not horizontally inward. Distractor 4 — air drag is far too small to provide centripetal force.
